purpose: The rail on small screens — the same AppSideNav, rendered inside an fds Drawer that slides over the page.

useInstead.use: AppSideNav directly — the drawer exists only below the breakpoint

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for the mobile nav drawer.
decision.beforeTheRules: This exists because the SDK's own mobile mode could not be used. SideNavBar renders its own MobileNav below 768px, but that drawer's open state lives inside the provider with no controlled prop — so the top bar, which is outside the provider, could never open it. The SDK's mobile breakpoint is disabled (`mobileBreakpoint={0}`) and this component replaces it.

rules.then: render this instead of AppSideNav, and render only one of the two
rules.because: both mounted at once puts two copies of every nav row in the tab order

rules.if: you are passing the rail into the drawer
rules.then: pass `isPinned` so it renders fully expanded
rules.because: a collapsed rail inside a drawer is an icon strip nobody asked for — the drawer already has room for labels

rules.if: the viewport crosses back above the breakpoint while the drawer is open
rules.because: otherwise a scroll lock is stranded on <body> with no visible control left to release it

rules.if: the reader follows a nav link inside the drawer
rules.because: they land on the new page with the drawer still covering it

constraints: The drawer needs an explicit height on its content: the SDK warns '[SideNavBarProvider] has zero height' otherwise, and the rail renders invisible.

accessibility.keyboard: Focus is trapped inside while open, returns to the trigger on close, and Escape closes it.
accessibility.aria: The drawer is a dialog; the rail inside keeps its own <nav aria-label="Main"> and aria-current.
accessibility.notes: The scrim is a mouse convenience and is aria-hidden — Escape and the close button are the accessible ways out.

composition.notes: DrawerBody is rendered with padding off, so the rail sits flush to the drawer's edges as it does on desktop.

antiPatterns.dont: Rendering AppSideNav and AppNavDrawer at the same time
antiPatterns.do: Switch on the breakpoint and render one
antiPatterns.why: every nav row ends up twice in the tab order, and screen readers announce two Main landmarks

antiPatterns.dont: Passing a collapsed rail into the drawer
antiPatterns.why: the drawer has room for labels; an icon strip inside it is a rail nobody chose

antiPatterns.dont: Leaving the drawer open across a resize to desktop
antiPatterns.do: Close it when isMobile goes false
antiPatterns.why: the body scroll lock survives and there is no longer a control on screen to release it

incorrect.why: one or the other — two mounted rails means two of every row in the tab order
